outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: AI-monetizing cloud infrastructure, led by Amazon's earnings
strongest.reason: Amazon jumped roughly 15% after AWS revenue growth accelerated to 36.7% and management flagged capacity constraints running into 2027-2028 — following Microsoft's own Azure beat the prior week, it's now two of the three major cloud players showing AI spend converting into accelerating revenue.

strongest.area: Enterprise software and cybersecurity earnings season
strongest.reason: Salesforce, ServiceNow (on a multi-day view), Adobe, CrowdStrike, and Fortinet have all posted solid results or beats this stretch, with CrowdStrike raising full-year guidance and Fortinet jumping over 12% on a billings beat.

weakest.area: Semiconductors, especially names reporting into the rout
weakest.reason: The sector has now shed roughly $1.3 trillion in value since last Friday on AI-capex sustainability worries and reports of Chinese progress in advanced chipmaking; AMD extended its slide heading into its August 4 earnings report, and Arm is still lagging despite last week's outright beat.

Bitcoin briefly dipped below $64,000 on renewed US-Iran tensions and a firmer dollar, with Ethereum lagging the modest bounce back; sector-specific overhangs (protocol exploits, an exchange trimming staff) are adding to the macro-driven softness.

outlook.nextStep: Amazon's AWS acceleration and capacity guidance is the most dated, verifiable data point available right now — worth a closer look at what's actually converting AI capex into revenue versus what isn't. The chip-sector rout and AMD's pre-earnings slide are noisier, sentiment-driven moves that are better watched than acted on until AMD reports on August 4.

signals.title: Markets keep digesting last week's divided Fed vote as labor-market data softens
signals.body: The FOMC's 9-3 split hold from July 29 continues to work through markets, with roughly three-quarters of officials now projecting little to no further rate change through the rest of 2026. Separately, recent labor-market readings have pointed to continued softening, with tariff-sensitive sectors showing job cuts and an employment gauge at its lowest level in months.
signals.watch: Whether upcoming labor-market data reinforces the softening trend, which would raise the odds of a rate cut later this year.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a softening labor market alongside a still-divided Fed is a more consequential combination than either signal alone.

signals.title: Amazon's AWS acceleration becomes the clearest AI-monetization data point yet
signals.body: Amazon shares jumped roughly 15% — their biggest move since 2012 — after AWS revenue grew 36.7% (a fifth straight quarter of acceleration) and management said AWS likely won't have enough capacity to meet demand through 2026 and probably 2027. Capex guidance was raised to roughly $220 billion for the year.
signals.watch: Whether Alphabet's own cloud numbers, due out shortly, tell a similar capacity-constrained story.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — two of the three hyperscalers now reporting accelerating cloud growth with explicit capacity constraints is a concrete, dated signal on AI demand.

signals.title: Chip-sector rout persists; AMD slides further heading into August 4 earnings
signals.body: The semiconductor sector has shed roughly $1.3 trillion in value since last Friday on renewed doubts about AI-capex sustainability and signs of Chinese progress in advanced chipmaking. AMD extended its multi-day slide ahead of its own earnings report due August 4, while Arm continues to lag despite last week's clean beat on revenue and EPS.
signals.watch: AMD's August 4 report as the next concrete data point — a strong beat that still gets sold would reinforce the sentiment-repricing read; a rally on a beat would suggest the selloff is closer to exhausted.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a broad, multi-day, cross-border rout with earnings beats getting sold anyway looks more like a valuation reset than a single clean catalyst.

signals.title: UBTECH pulls back after its recent humanoid-component-driven run
signals.body: UBTECH Robotics gave back roughly 5% after a stretch of gains tied to broader optimism around humanoid-robot component suppliers. Teradyne and Intuitive Surgical both held roughly steady, still working through the aftermath of their respective earnings reactions.
signals.watch: Whether the pullback in UBTECH is isolated profit-taking or the start of a broader cooldown across humanoid-component names.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a single-name pullback after a sharp run is more consistent with profit-taking than a change in the underlying thesis, but it's worth confirming with the next few sessions.

signals.title: Cybersecurity earnings season delivers mostly strong results, testing the sector's rich valuations
signals.body: CrowdStrike posted 25.6% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance, Fortinet jumped over 12% on a billings beat, and SentinelOne came in roughly in line with estimates. The sector's average price-to-earnings ratio remains near 90 after a strong multi-month rally, keeping the bar high for the remaining reports in this earnings window.
signals.watch: Whether the remaining names in this earnings window can match CrowdStrike and Fortinet's results, or whether the group starts trading down even on beats the way chips have.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a cluster of same-window beats with a guidance raise is one of the more dated, verifiable signals available in this tier right now.

signals.title: Bitcoin dips below $64,000 on renewed US-Iran tensions and dollar strength
signals.body: Bitcoin briefly fell below $64,000 as renewed Middle East tensions lifted oil prices and strengthened the dollar, before stabilizing modestly. Ethereum lagged the bounce. Separately, Circle secured a New York trust charter allowing it to offer fiduciary and custody services for USDC, while reports flagged over $330 million in losses across Ethereum-based projects this year from protocol vulnerabilities.
signals.watch: Whether the macro-driven dip resolves like prior post-Fed dips have, and whether the protocol-vulnerability losses prompt any broader risk repricing in DeFi-adjacent tokens.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a geopolitically-driven dip layered on top of sector-specific security concerns is a noisier setup than a single clean catalyst.
